newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai says Sega merger off on lack of synergy.
newsitem.headline: Bandai says Sega merger off on lack of synergy.

text.p: In a last-minute cancellation of what was to become the birth of Japan's Disney, Bandai Co Ltd said on Tuesday that they called off their merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd because it lacked synergy.
"We could not see a clear picture of the synergy, which is, after all, the purpose of a merger," Bandai president Makoto Yamashina told reporters.
It said instead of the merger, the two companies would pursue a business tie-up covering character entertainment and retailing, consumer products, manufacturing and distribution.

The surprise announcement came only a day before the two firms were due to approve a merger pact, slated to take effect on October 1, and a day after toymaker Bandai had called a news conference to confirm it was still on board with the merger.

Sega, maker of the Sega Saturn 32-bit video-game player, and Bandai, known for its Power Rangers and virtual pet toy "Tamagotchi", said in January that they would merge to create a global entertainment giant likened to Walt Disney Co.
Sega President Hayao Nakayama told a separate news conference that the abrupt cancellation was in response to Bandai's proposal for an annullment earlier on Tuesday.

"It appears that among (Bandai's) younger-generation management class, the true purpose of the merger had not hit home and only the negative aspects -- such as the fact that Bandai would be absorbed in the merger -- had sunk in," he said.

He added that in a company like Bandai, which has its strength in developing characters and ideas such as Tamagotchi, "there is no point in pursuing something that the younger managers cannot get excited about."
"That's why we accepted the cancellation," Nakayama said.

Speculation had already been rife prior to the break-up announcement that the merger could be delayed due to strong opposition from mid-level managers at Bandai, a closely-knit toymaker heartened by its recent runaway hit on Tamagotchi.

On Monday, a Bandai executive called a sudden news conference to say that the company expected its board to approve the merger with Sega at a meeting on Wednesday, withdrawing an earlier plan to postpone approval until July.
Bandai managing director Mikio Ishigami told reporters that employees were "extremely nervous" about the environment change, but that he was confident they would come on board.
On Tuesday, Bandai president Yamashina said there were "huge differences in the two corporate cultures."
Although accepting responsibility for the bungling of the deal, Yamashina said he had no plans to resign to atone for it.

Analysts said the cancellation announcement, which came after the Tokyo stock market closed, would be negative for the two firms, although they were split over which company had more to lose from the failed deal.

"They had repeatedly said that there would be no future without a merger. The cancellation would be taken as negative, especially for Bandai," said Yasuo Imanaka, an analyst at Okasan Economic Research Institute. "Bandai cannot expect much business expansion with its current domestic operations alone."
Hironobu Sawaki, analyst at Nikko Research Centre, said the cancellation could have a negative impact on Sega's share prices, while the impact would be neutral for Bandai.
"Sega would have acquired much-wanted distribution routes for children's goods and Bandai's sales know-how," he said.
On Tuesday, both companies' shares fell, with Sega sliding 20 yen to close at 3,700 yen and Bandai dropping 30 yen to end at 2,760 yen.
The two companies were due to announce earnings results on Wednesday for fiscal year 1996/97.
